about_feature_fast_dev_desc: Vite keeps iteration tight so route, style, and server changes are quick to verify.
about_feature_responsive_desc: The layouts are built to hold together on narrow screens without turning dense.
about_feature_type_safety_desc: Typed boundaries across routes, loaders, actions, and RPC keep the demo honest.
about_features_intro: The goal is not visual noise or framework gymnastics — it is a readable demo surface with fast iteration and clear behavior.
about_hero_body: This demo keeps the stack intentionally compact so React Router, Hono, Vanilla Extract, and typed request flows stay easy to inspect instead of disappearing behind abstraction.
about_hero_lead: Architecture, stack, and design decisions in one place.
about_next_errors_desc: See boundaries, status codes, and recovery behavior under failure conditions.
about_next_hono_rpc_desc: Follow the typed client and server exchange through the Hono RPC demo.
about_next_intro: After the overview, use the remaining routes to inspect rendering, data flow, and failure handling in isolation.
about_next_ssr_desc: Inspect request-time rendering and timing data on a server-owned page.
about_stack_frontend_desc: The interface layer keeps routing, components, styling, and iconography easy to inspect.
about_stack_intro: Rather than hide the app behind heavy framework chrome, each layer is exposed clearly so you can read how the demo is assembled.
about_stack_runtime_desc: The server side stays deliberately small so rendering and request flow are visible instead of hidden.
about_stack_title: The stack stays small so the ideas stay visible.
error_code_default_detail: This route formats both thrown responses and runtime exceptions into a consistent SSR error view.
error_code_default_scenario_note: This code path is not part of the curated examples.
error_code_default_summary: The loader intentionally failed so the route boundary could take over.
error_code_footer_note: Thrown responses preserve their HTTP semantics; thrown runtime errors are still caught here, but the boundary presents them as an application failure.
error_code_pending_message: This route is designed to throw before the normal component renders
error_code_row_1_body: The boundary normalized the thrown value into a readable status surface.
error_code_row_2_body: The error starts in the route loader and finishes in the route boundary.
error_code_row_3_body: Compare different routes to see how the boundary behaves across status families.
error_code_section_intro: This route throws in the loader, then the route-level boundary renders the final page you are seeing now.
error_code_value_rendered_by: ErrorBoundary in the same route file
error_scenario_401_detail: Simulates a protected route where credentials are required before the request can continue.
error_scenario_401_summary: A request was understood, but the user is not authenticated.
error_scenario_403_detail: Shows the difference between being unauthenticated and being blocked after authentication.
error_scenario_403_summary: The request is known, but the current actor is not allowed to proceed.
error_scenario_404_detail: Throws a 404 `Response` so the route boundary can render a missing-resource state.
error_scenario_404_summary: Use this when a path or resource should report that it does not exist.
error_scenario_500_detail: Models an internal server failure where the route cannot produce a normal response.
error_scenario_500_summary: A generic server-side failure became an HTTP error response.
error_scenario_502_detail: Represents an upstream dependency that answered incorrectly or with unusable data.
error_scenario_502_summary: The app responded, but one dependency upstream failed first.
error_scenario_503_detail: Useful for downtime and maintenance states where the route should advertise temporary unavailability.
error_scenario_503_summary: The service is alive enough to answer, but not ready to fulfill the request.
error_scenario_runtime_detail: Throws a normal JavaScript error instead of a `Response`, which lets you compare the two failure shapes. The server-side log keeps the current `app.session_id` so you can match it to the browser issue.
error_scenario_runtime_summary: A runtime exception escaped the route logic and was caught by the route boundary.
errors_hero_body: Use this page to jump into thrown response errors, runtime exceptions, and the route boundaries that present them. The hub itself is prerendered; each case underneath is a live server-rendered incident surface.
errors_hero_lead: A static index for the failure paths the app can intentionally trigger.
errors_notice_1_body: `/errors` is safe to prerender because it never throws.
errors_notice_1_detail: It works as a navigational map into the error cases rather than an error screen itself.
errors_notice_2_body: `/errors/:code` throws from the loader to simulate real failures.
errors_notice_2_detail: That makes the page useful for seeing how SSR, status codes, and response headers behave when a route does not resolve normally.
errors_notice_3_body: The route boundary catches the failure and turns it into the final visual surface.
errors_notice_3_detail: That means the page you see for `404`, `500`, or `runtime` is intentionally designed by the route, not by a browser fallback.
errors_section_intro_choose: Every route below demonstrates a different way the app can fail and how the route-level boundary reshapes that failure into something inspectable.
errors_section_intro_notice: The interesting split is between the static entry page, the dynamic route loader, and the boundary that formats both response errors and thrown exceptions.
errors_spacer_intro: Start with `/errors/404` or `/errors/runtime` to compare a thrown response with a thrown JavaScript error.
hero_body: Five routes keep SSR, RPC, layout, boundaries, and architecture legible without turning the homepage into a dashboard.
hero_lead: Render, route, and recover with a compact full-stack demo.
holy_grail_article_desc: The root keeps the document skeleton. This route owns the visible structure, so the holy grail pattern stays local to the page instead of leaking into the app shell.
holy_grail_article_title: Header on top, main in the middle, footer at the bottom.
holy_grail_footer_note: Static route • prerendered at build time • no loader required
holy_grail_layout_main_desc: The middle track expands and remains readable at every width.
holy_grail_layout_note_1: The document shell stays in root.tsx.
holy_grail_layout_note_2: The page shell is a grid with header, main, and footer rows.
holy_grail_layout_note_3: The middle track uses grid columns so the sidebars never steal the spotlight.
holy_grail_layout_right_desc: Status, notes, and related links that should not dominate the flow.
holy_grail_left_desc: This column keeps the supporting information close without asking the main content to carry everything.
holy_grail_left_note_1: Persistent navigation stays out of the main reading flow.
holy_grail_left_note_2: Useful metadata belongs in the rail, not in the hero copy.
holy_grail_left_note_3: The layout still works when the rails collapse on mobile.
holy_grail_nested_desc: The nested shell lets the middle track adapt to the article width instead of the viewport.
holy_grail_nested_title: Header, main, footer inside the article.
holy_grail_right_desc: The side rail is where you place references, status, or helper content without forcing the central article to do double duty.
holy_grail_right_note_1: Sticky sidebars create the classic holy grail silhouette.
holy_grail_right_note_2: The center column is the only region that should stretch hard.
holy_grail_right_note_3: Header and footer frame the content without boxing it in.
hono_rpc_error_retry: Try reloading the Hono RPC page
hono_rpc_hero_body: The initial response comes through the route loader, then the same endpoint can be revalidated on the client through the Hono RPC client.
hono_rpc_hero_lead: A typed request surface that refreshes without leaving the route.
hono_rpc_label_initial_source_value: Route loader / shared API response factory
hono_rpc_row_1_body: Values returned from `GET /api/rpc/hello`, rendered first by the loader and then refreshed on demand.
hono_rpc_row_2_body: The route and API stay connected through the generated Hono client instead of manual fetch strings.
hono_rpc_row_3_body: The page is built to show where SSG, hydration, revalidation, and typed API calls intersect.
hono_rpc_section_intro: The same typed endpoint powers the initial route load and the in-page refresh action.
hono_rpc_section_title: The response is live and re-fetchable.
hono_rpc_value_client_refresh: The button fetches fresh RPC data without reloading the page.
hono_rpc_value_hydrated_data: The initial server-rendered response stays visible while the client can fetch fresh data on demand.
hono_rpc_value_prerendered_shell: The route can ship static structure at build time.
hono_rpc_value_typed_boundary: The `hc()` client keeps route code aligned with the API contract.
labs_hero_body: Each lab is a self-contained tool built on a shared Rust kernel: the browser runs it as WASM, and heavy renders are offloaded to a Rust Cloudflare Worker at the edge. More labs are on the way.
labs_hero_lead: Interactive tools compiled from Rust to WebAssembly.
labs_mandelbrot_canvas_desc: Hold Ctrl (or ⌘) and scroll to zoom, drag to pan. Switch the engine — JavaScript, Rust WASM, or WebGL2 GPU — to see how each frame is produced.
labs_mandelbrot_edge_desc: The same viewport is rendered at 1920×1080 by the fractal-rust Cloudflare Worker and returned as a PNG. The render time comes from the x-render-time-ms response header.
labs_mandelbrot_footer_note_1: The interactive canvas runs the shared kernel from
labs_mandelbrot_footer_note_2: compiled to WASM; the edge render is served by the
labs_mandelbrot_gpu_note: The GPU path computes in 32-bit floats, so very deep zooms may show slight banding — the CPU paths stay exact.
labs_mandelbrot_hero_body: One Rust kernel, two runtimes: the browser executes it as WASM for the interactive canvas, while a Rust Cloudflare Worker renders high-resolution PNGs at the edge. Race it against JavaScript to see the difference.
labs_mandelbrot_hero_lead: Rust compiled to WASM, running in your browser and at the edge.
labs_mandelbrot_race_desc: The same viewport rendered by the TypeScript baseline, the Rust WASM module, and the GPU, back to back. Timings are measured in your browser.
labs_mandelbrot_status_error: Failed to load the WASM module. Build it with: deno task build:fractal-wasm
labs_more_note: More labs are being built — the shared kernel in packages/fractal-wasm keeps each new tool a small increment.
labs_section_intro: Pick a tool. Each one is a standalone page built on the same shared Rust kernel.
labs_tool_mandelbrot_desc: Zoom a fractal rendered by WASM, race JavaScript against Rust, and render high-resolution PNGs on the edge.

route_about_description: Project overview, stack notes, and the migration decisions behind the app.

routes_section_intro: Each entry isolates one concern so you can inspect the stack in pieces instead of decoding everything at once.
routes_section_title: Start with one route. The rest stays in view.
ssr_hero_body: The loader runs on each request, forwards timing metadata, and can read Hono context before the page reaches the browser.
ssr_hero_lead: This route renders on the server for every visit.
ssr_hono_context_desc: Data forwarded from the Hono request context into the React Router loader through `RouterContextProvider`.
ssr_live_response_desc: Request-specific data produced by the SSR loader before the page is delivered.
ssr_loader_message: This page is rendered on the server on EVERY request!
ssr_section_response_intro: These values are generated during the request, then serialized into the rendered HTML and response headers.
ssr_section_response_title: The current response came from the server.
ssr_section_verify_intro: The route is meant to be inspected, not just viewed. These checks make the rendering mode obvious.
ssr_section_verify_title: How to verify the page is really SSR.
ssr_verify_compare_value: Unlike `/` or `/about`, this route is not SSG. Unlike CSR-only UI, its first HTML already contains the server response.
ssr_verify_desc: Use the browser and network tooling to confirm the response is generated at request time.
ssr_verify_headers_value: Open the Network tab and check `Server-Timing` to verify the loader duration.
ssr_verify_refresh_value: The timestamp changes on every request because the loader runs server-side each time.
